Theme

School & learning · Household, washing & chores

chemical noun

a chemical substance

also chemicals, chemical substance, chemical product

modern

Traupman 165, 290
M-O s.v. chemical (Pharm. Nosocom.)

1chēmicum: long e (Traupman 165 leaves it unmarked). Greek χημεία, with eta; Morgan–Owens s.v. chemistry writes chêmicus. See chemical (adjective).

chēmicum1, chēmicī n.

noun, second declension

a chemical

The adjective used as a noun; plural chēmica, chemicals.

Other words

  • māteria chēmica — a chemical substance

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. chemical (Egger)

  • medicāmentum, medicāmentī n. — a drug, a prepared substance: medicine, poison, dye

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.92 (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 27.101: medicāmentō sagittās tingere (Lewis & Short)

    The classical word nearest to “a chemical”: any prepared substance that acts on a thing, as a remedy, a poison or a dye (Lewis & Short). Its usual sense is a medicine (see medicine); use it for a chemical only where the context shows it.

See also chemical, medicine, science.

SourcesLewis & Short: medicamentum

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 165, 290. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. chemical, chemistry.

Lewis & Short has no entry for chemicum.
